result.note: An official trade data release. The questions test the direction and composition of May 2026 trade and the bullion import duty hike.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's trade data for May 2026, released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry in June 2026:
items: Total exports of merchandise and services were estimated at USD 81.96 billion, up 15.83% on a year earlier.
The combined trade deficit narrowed compared with May 2025.
Petroleum products led the growth in merchandise exports.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the combined trade deficit widened to USD 10.51 billion from USD 6.79 billion, as imports grew 19.23% to USD 92.47 billion. Petroleum products rose 54.89% and engineering goods 24.48%, together leading merchandise exports to USD 45.20 billion.
questions.source: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry estimated total exports of merchandise and services at USD 81.96 billion for May 2026, up 15.83% on a year earlier, even as the combined trade deficit widened to USD 10.51 billion from USD 6.79 billion.

questions.prompt: As reported in June 2026, the Centre had raised the effective import duty on gold and silver to what level, in order to curb dollar outflows on bullion?
questions.explain: The effective duty on gold and silver imports was raised to 15% from 6% to curb dollar outflows on bullion. The merchandise trade deficit alone reached USD 28.21 billion in May 2026.
questions.source: The Centre had raised the effective gold and silver import duty to 15% from 6%, aimed at curbing dollar outflows on bullion
